solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Try and catch fish with special instrument

parts.note: a fisherman throwing his mesh into the water to attempt a haul is said to cast a net

explanation.surface: An angler tries to catch fish with some special piece of gear.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening phrase works as one unit: what you do when you try to catch fish is CAST A NET, run together. 'with' just joins on S.
explanation.definitionFit: The paired wooden clappers of Spanish dance count as a single percussion instrument.

clue.text: Recording includes noise of gate

indicators.note: the recording holds the noise within it, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a CD, compact disc, is a recording
a row is a loud din or noise

explanation.surface: A recording picks up the racket of a garden gate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gate' is not a garden gate but the attendance at a sports match, a British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: In British sport the gate is the number of spectators attending, i.e. the size of the throng.

clue.text: Complaint that wrong American protest is cut short and rejected

parts.note: a sin is a wrong

indicators.note: rejected means the shortened protest is turned back to front
cut short means the last letter of the protest word is lopped off

parts.note: a sit-in is a protest occupying a place

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles that a wrongful American protest was curtailed and turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complaint' sounds like a grievance, matching the protest story, but means an illness; 'cut short' and 'rejected' act in turn on the sit-in.
explanation.definitionFit: Inflamed nasal sinuses are a common medical complaint, i.e. an ailment.

clue.text: London palace covers current library site

indicators.note: covers means the palace wraps around the current symbol

parts.note: Alexandra Palace, 'Ally Pally', is a famous entertainment venue in north London
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A London palace covers the current site of a library.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current' looks like 'present-day' but is the physics symbol I. Alexandra Palace is a London landmark, birthplace of BBC television.
explanation.definitionFit: The Egyptian city was home to the great Library of the ancient world.

clue.text: Building in Crete a dubious attraction

indicators.note: building means the letters of 'in Crete' are put together in a new construction

explanation.surface: A building in Crete is a questionable tourist draw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Building' reads as a noun but is the anagram signal on IN CRETE.
explanation.definitionFit: A tempter or lure draws people in, often towards something shady, hence a dubious attraction.

clue.text: Exhibitors' point accepted by blacksmiths

indicators.note: accepted by means the point goes inside the blacksmiths' word

parts.note: blacksmiths who fit horseshoes are shoers
W, west, is a compass point

explanation.surface: At a trade fair, the exhibitors' argument is accepted by the blacksmiths.
explanation.walkthrough: 'point' looks like an argument but is a compass point, W.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who display or present things are people who show them, i.e. exhibitors.

clue.text: Shrink bird

definitions.meaning: to cower or flinch back in fear
a small game bird related to the partridge

explanation.surface: A psychiatrist who is a bird, or a bird that shrinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shrink' tempts as the noun for a psychiatrist; here it is the verb to cower.
explanation.definitionFit: To recoil in fear is one sense; the other is a small plump game bird.

clue.text: Four-footer throws away fruit, stoned in courtyard

indicators.note: throws away means the fruit's letters are removed from the animal word

parts.note: a four-footed animal is a quadruped
a drupe is a fruit with a stone, like a plum or cherry

explanation.surface: An animal discards fruit after removing the stones in a courtyard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stoned' does not mean pitted: a fruit with a stone is a DRUPE, taken from QUADRUPED.
explanation.definitionFit: A quadrangle, the enclosed courtyard of a college, is shortened to this word.

clue.text: Hebrew character's beer bar

parts.note: ale is beer
PH, public house, is a bar

explanation.surface: A Jewish character's local is a beer bar.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the first letter of the Hebrew alphabet, so a written character.

clue.text: Post office facility gets improved security from Spooner

indicators.note: Rev Spooner swapped the opening sounds of word pairs, so these two words trade their first consonants

parts.note: better means improved
locks provide security

explanation.surface: A post office installs better security measures.
explanation.walkthrough: BETTER LOCKS with the B and L swapped gives LETTER BOCKS, which sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A slot or box for posting mail is a basic postal facility.

clue.text: Cat club official takes off clothes

indicators.note: taking off clothes strips the outer covering, so the first and last letters go

parts.note: a bouncer guards a nightclub door

explanation.surface: A cat club official strips off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes off clothes' strips the outer letters B and R from BOUNCER.
explanation.definitionFit: The snow leopard is also known by this name, a large wild feline.

clue.text: Heading for Oklahoma, war god's chariot finally broke

parts.note: heading for means going to
OK is the postal abbreviation for Oklahoma
Ares is the Greek god of war

indicators.note: finally signals the last letter of chariot

explanation.surface: The war god's chariot broke down on the way to Oklahoma.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broke' is not 'smashed' or 'penniless' but 'had a break'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pausing from work to relax is taking a break, a phrase for having stopped.

clue.text: Slain director yearned to go round resort

indicators.note: to go round means the yearning word encloses the resort

parts.note: itched means longed or yearned
a spa is a health resort

explanation.surface: A director longed to tour a resort and was killed.
explanation.definitionFit: To be killed off or put to death is to be finished, i.e. slain.

clue.text: Cooking medium gas found in Georgia

indicators.note: found in means the gas sits inside the Georgia abbreviation

parts.note: GE is the code for the country of Georgia
He is the chemical symbol for helium, a gas

explanation.surface: A cooking fuel, gas, is discovered in Georgia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'medium' is not a fortune-teller: it is what food is cooked in.
explanation.definitionFit: Clarified butter used in Indian cooking is a fat in which food is fried.

clue.text: Put pressure on about handling uncovered fishing equipment

indicators.note: about means the pressure word is wrapped around the handling letters

parts.note: to ride someone is to keep putting pressure on them; 'put' is past tense, so rode

indicators.note: uncovered strips the first and last letters off handling

explanation.surface: Someone was pressured over their handling of the fishing kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put' is past tense, so RODE; 'uncovered' takes ANDLIN from 'handling'.
explanation.definitionFit: An angler's pole with its cord is the classic tackle for catching fish.

clue.text: Animal killer a bit overwhelmed by recovered memory

indicators.note: overwhelmed by means the small amount is engulfed inside the memory word
recovered here means covered again from the other side: the memory word is read backwards

parts.note: ROM, read-only memory, is computer memory
a tad is a little bit

explanation.surface: An animal killer, a little overcome by a recovered memory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recovered' reads as retrieved, but here the computer memory is turned around before it engulfs 'a bit'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bullfighter is the one who kills the bull in the ring, so a slayer of animals.

clue.text: Cause trouble for mother with garden birds

parts.note: ma is mother
Kew Gardens is the Royal Botanic Gardens in west London
Aves is the scientific class of birds

explanation.surface: Causing trouble for mother with birds in the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: KEW is the famous botanic garden in London; AVES is Latin for birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Stirring things up or creating disturbance is the idiom for causing trouble.

clue.text: Attempt to deceive ski instructor?

definitions.meaning: a smooth persuasive con or deception
whimsically, someone whose employment is on the white stuff on slopes

explanation.surface: Trying to fool a ski instructor.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful second reading: a job in the snow.
explanation.definitionFit: American slang for flattering deception; literally a piece of work on the white stuff.

clue.text: Bench-warmer people ultimately exhibit good sense

parts.note: a judge sits on the bench, warming it
men means people

indicators.note: ultimately signals the last letter of exhibit

explanation.surface: A substitute sports player shows good sense in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bench-warmer' suggests a sports substitute but is a judge on the court bench.
explanation.definitionFit: Sound discernment and wisdom in decisions is what good sense is.

clue.text: Just touching American statesman once gets rid of I don't know what

indicators.note: gets rid of means the hesitation letters are removed

parts.note: Henry Kissinger was US Secretary of State
er is a hesitating sound expressing uncertainty

explanation.surface: A former American statesman discards something unknown that was just touching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I don't know what' is ER, the sound of hesitation, dropped from KISSINGER.
explanation.definitionFit: Snooker and billiards balls resting in contact are said to be in this state, barely in contact.

clue.text: Mechanics here a long time after fish

indicators.note: after means the long time follows the fish

parts.note: gar is a long-snouted fish
ages means a long time

explanation.surface: Mechanics took a long time after the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Car repair shops are where mechanics work, so the places they would be found.

clue.text: Congress holds on to power with elastic fibre

indicators.note: holds on to means the congress word keeps the other pieces inside it

parts.note: sexual congress, so sex
P is the symbol for power
and means with

explanation.surface: The US Congress clings on to power with stretchy material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Congress' is not the legislature but its old sense of intercourse.
explanation.definitionFit: Lycra-type stretch fabric is a synthetic elastic fibre.

clue.text: Drops come out of second golf club

parts.note: a putter is a golf club for the green

explanation.surface: A golfer's second club is dropped from the bag.
explanation.definitionFit: To spit out little bursts of liquid in spluttering fashion is to eject drops.

clue.text: Left in the middle of this

indicators.note: in the middle of means only the inner part of the number is kept, with its ends dropped

parts.note: this clue is number 20, so 'this' stands for twenty

explanation.surface: Something left in the middle of this.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this' refers to the clue's own number, 20, written out; the middle of TWENTY remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Departed is the past tense of go, so a synonym for left.

clue.text: Shark runs around on earth

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece on another sits above it
around means the letters of runs are moved round into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
E is the abbreviation for earth in electrical wiring

explanation.surface: A shark swims around on earth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shark' could be a swindler, but here the fish is meant; 'around' rearranges 'runs', which sits above the earth letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A type of slow bottom-dwelling shark of warm seas carries this name.

clue.text: Empty gasometer under zoo damaged where the bomb went off

indicators.note: empty means hollowing out the gasometer, keeping only its outer letters
damaged means the letters of 'under zoo' are wrecked and reassembled

explanation.surface: A gasometer, empty and sitting below a damaged zoo, marks the blast site.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Empty' keeps G and R; 'damaged' rearranges UNDER ZOO into OUNDZERO.
explanation.definitionFit: The point directly beneath a nuclear blast is the term for the explosion's hypocentre.

clue.text: Youth body journalist exposed

indicators.note: the body of a word is its central part, without its head and tail

parts.note: ED, editor, is a journalist

explanation.surface: A youth organisation's journalist was exposed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Youth body' suggests an organisation; it is the middle of 'Youth', OUT.
explanation.definitionFit: To have someone's secret, such as sexuality, revealed publicly is to be exposed.

clue.text: Missed target as sloth escaped and ran away

indicators.note: escaped means the sloth's letters get out of the failure word

parts.note: to miss a target is to have failed
the ai is a three-toed sloth

explanation.surface: Missing its target as a sloth escaped and ran away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sloth' is not laziness but the animal AI, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: To flee is to run away; this is its past tense.

clue.text: Flare less than one 9?

definitions.meaning: a coloured signal flare fired from a pistol
9-across is an ounce, so something weighing under one is extremely low in weight

explanation.surface: A flare weighing less than one cat.
explanation.walkthrough: The 9 points to 9-across, OUNCE; the second reading is a whimsical description of weight.
explanation.definitionFit: A Very light is a pistol-fired signal flare; read differently it means hardly weighing anything.

clue.text: Fancy tiepin I lost being clumsy

indicators.note: fancy means the remaining letters are elaborately rearranged
lost means the letter I is dropped from the tiepin

explanation.surface: I lost a fancy tiepin through clumsiness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' removes one I from TIEPIN; 'Fancy' rearranges TEPIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking skill or deftness, being awkward and incompetent.

clue.text: Avenger's way to get river flowing backwards

parts.note: ST, street, is a way

indicators.note: flowing backwards means the river's name is read in reverse

parts.note: the Dee is a British river

explanation.surface: An avenger's route to a river that flows the wrong way.
explanation.walkthrough: John Steed is the bowler-hatted hero of the 1960s British TV series The Avengers.
explanation.definitionFit: John Steed was the gentleman agent of the British spy show The Avengers.

clue.text: Scattered fruit seed filled to bursting

indicators.note: scattered means the letters of 'fruit seed' are strewn into a new order

explanation.surface: Scattered fruit seed fills a container until it bursts.
explanation.definitionFit: Overfed or glutted until one can hold no more, sated to excess.
